title: Exact closed restriction on arbitrary element sites
statement: For a commutative ring sheaf R, actual element restriction has a natural derived internal-Hom comparison. Further restriction along every sheaf arrow admits the exact additive, K-injective, unit and derived-Hom data of RingedPresentationCore, with identity unit. For each site object U the module category on C/U is equivalent to the module category on the element site of the sheafified representable of U; its forward unit and derived Hom are compatible and the usual overFunctor corresponds to element restriction. Actual restriction additivity, exactness, colimits, K-injectivity, element-map continuity and relocalization are already proved in RingedPresentationData and are not asserted as unfinished parts here.

proof.text: For a functor whose induced functors on all over categories are equivalences, precomposition gives a bijection on restricted module morphisms. Lift the underlying abelian-group natural transformation through the equivalence and prove linearity using essential surjectivity. These bijections yield a sectionwise sheaf-Hom isomorphism, natural in both variables.

Restriction preserves integer-indexed products, as seen after the limit-reflecting forgetful functor to abelian presheaves. Compare Hom complexes by their product projections. The projection differential formula and naturality of the sheaf-Hom comparison prove compatibility with the signed differential and with both complex variables.

Compute derived Hom using the canonical functorial K-injective resolutions. Compare the restricted resolution with the resolution of the restricted complex through a common resolution. Their natural quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives induce isomorphisms of Hom complexes after localization. Fully faithful whiskering by the product localization descends the resulting natural isomorphism. Apply this to the element projection, whose over-category functors are equivalences, using the existing exactness and K-injective API.

For B→A construct the fibre sheaf on the element site of A, using the specified element-site fibre equivalence to verify its sheaf property. Flatten its iterated element category to the element category of B and prove this is an equivalence of sites by the covering-sieve formula. The continuous-cocontinuous ringed restriction and ringed module-equivalence theorem identify module restriction with this equivalence. Transport exactness, sequential colimits and K-injectivity from ordinary element restriction. The over-category equivalence for B→A follows by cancellation from those of the two projections, so the generic derived-Hom comparison applies. The regular-module unit is definitionally the identity.

For U construct C/U→Elements(h_U#) by sending a→U to its sheafification section. It is faithful, cover-dense by local surjectivity of the sheafification unit, and locally full by local injectivity of that unit. Its image sieves cover exactly when the original slice sieves cover. The dense-subsite equivalence and continuous-cocontinuous ringed restriction give the closed module equivalence by the ringed-equivalence theorem. Reverse that equivalence and its derived-Hom comparison. The composite with ordinary restriction agrees sectionwise with element restriction, giving the required natural isomorphism.

theorem element_restriction_hom
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) :
    ∃ (s : ∀ {A B : Sheaf J (Type u)} (b : B ⟶ A),
        RingedPresentationCore (presentationElementRing R A) (presentationElementRing R B)
          (elementModulePullbackOver.{u, u} (localCoefficientRings R) b
            (presentationElementRestriction_continuous b))),
      (∀ A : Sheaf J (Type u),
        Nonempty (presentationRHom R ⋙
          presentationDerivedMap (R := R) (S := presentationElementRing R A)
            (elementModulePullback.{u, u} (localCoefficientRings R) A)
            (presentationElementRestriction_additive R A)
            (presentationElementRestriction_exact R A).1
            (presentationElementRestriction_exact R A).2.1 ≅
          ((presentationDerivedMap (R := R) (S := presentationElementRing R A)
            (elementModulePullback.{u, u} (localCoefficientRings R) A)
              (presentationElementRestriction_additive R A)
              (presentationElementRestriction_exact R A).1
              (presentationElementRestriction_exact R A).2.1).op.prod
            (presentationDerivedMap (R := R) (S := presentationElementRing R A)
            (elementModulePullback.{u, u} (localCoefficientRings R) A)
              (presentationElementRestriction_additive R A)
              (presentationElementRestriction_exact R A).1
              (presentationElementRestriction_exact R A).2.1)) ⋙
            presentationRHom (presentationElementRing R A))) ∧
      (∀ {A B : Sheaf J (Type u)} (b : B ⟶ A), (s b).unit = Iso.refl _) ∧
      ∀ U : C,
        ∃ E : RingedPresentationEquivalenceCore (R.over U)
          (presentationElementRing R ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).obj (yoneda.obj U))),
          Nonempty (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (localCoefficientRings R) U ⋙
            E.modules.functor ≅ elementModulePullback.{u, u} (localCoefficientRings R)
              ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).obj (yoneda.obj U)))
